title: Tamsin and the Orbit
premise: Fifteen years after the Meridian Station massacre was erased from every record, cargo hauler Silas Whitlock finds a name on a manifest that shouldn't exist — Tamsin, daughter of the station's last engineer, alive and hiding in the contested orbit where her family died. Together with Silas's ragtag crew, Tamsin must recover the station's buried black box and broadcast the truth before the corporate fleet finishes scrubbing the sector. But proving the massacre means surrendering the only evidence keeping her hidden, forcing her to choose between survival and inheritance. In the end, the truth goes out at terrible cost: Silas loses his ship and nearly his life, but Tamsin gains a found family — and the dead of Meridian finally get their names back.
about_author: Marguerite Eastwick is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to voices cross empty water before turning to fiction about people crossing emptier space. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Atlantic coast.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Silas Whitlock, POV. Hauling freight through the contested Kestrel Orbit, Silas audits a decommissioned ship's ghost manifest and finds one live name: Tamsin Voss, listed as crew on a vessel that never launched. The discovery unsettles him more than any debt he owes. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine — the past knocking through paperwork.

chapters.title: A Girl in the Cargo Bay
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She stows away aboard Silas's hauler, the Long Answer, having tracked the manifest error herself — it's the only proof she exists. When Silas finds her, she offers the one thing she has: fragments of her father's final transmission from Meridian Station. Emotional beat: wary negotiation between two people who trust no one.

chapters.title: Dreams in Dead Languages
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. He decodes the transmission fragments using xenolinguistic methods he learned studying a species that records grief in structure rather than words. The fragments describe an attack — but official records show Meridian evacuated peacefully. His crew debates walking away. Emotional beat: the cost of knowing things you can't un-know.

chapters.title: Crew of the Long Answer
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating close-third POVs. Engineer Okafor patches the failing drive; pilot Reyes gambles their fuel margin; medic Juno quietly runs Tamsin's biometrics and realizes she's been living on station rations for years. Tamsin begins, reluctantly, to belong. Emotional beat: found family forming in the cracks of a broken ship.

chapters.title: The Scrubbers
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A corporate audit vessel hails them; the crew improvises a cover story while Tamsin hides in a coolant tank. She learns the fleet is systematically wiping Kestrel Orbit records — someone is finishing the job. First direct threat. Emotional beat: claustrophobic terror, and the realization that silence is being manufactured.

chapters.title: What Her Father Built
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Following engineering clues in the transmission, they locate Meridian's derelict backup core drifting in a debris shoal. Inside, Tamsin finds her father's workshop preserved — and a message addressed to whoever came looking. He knew he might not survive. Emotional beat: grief and inheritance intertwined; the weight of what parents leave behind.

chapters.title: Black Box
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They extract the black box containing full sensor logs of the massacre — but triggering its retrieval beacon alerts the corporate fleet. Okafor is injured covering the retreat. The crew must now run, not hide. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into consequence; evidence gained, safety lost.

chapters.title: Every Record Says Otherwise
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Hunted across the orbit, they seek a broadcaster powerful enough to pierce the sector's jamming net — an old relay run by Silas's estranged mentor, Ada Quill, who helped bury the original records and owes a debt. Confrontation, confession, uneasy alliance. Emotional beat: accountability demanded and grudgingly given.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, climax. Under fire, they patch the black box into the relay. Tamsin reads the victims' names aloud — her family among them — as the fleet tries to burn the relay down. Silas takes a hull breach getting the antenna aligned. The truth transmits sector-wide just as the Long Answer goes dark. Emotional beat: sacrifice, fury, and voice reclaimed.

chapters.title: Names Returned
chapters.summary: Ensemble, resolution. Weeks later: the broadcast forces an inquiry; survivors' families begin arriving in Kestrel Orbit. Silas recovers aboard a borrowed ship, the Long Answer lost but her crew intact. Tamsin, no longer a ghost on a manifest, signs on as crew under her own name. Emotional beat: mourning turned to memorial; survival's price paid, and worth it.
